results.title: GPU rental without hyperscalers: How good are neo clouds?
results.author: Benedikt Langer
highlights:
At Lambda, an H100 GPU costs 3.55 euros an hour, against 10.95 euros at Azure, according to the price list of 4 October 2026. Neo clouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius and Lambda offer another option alongside hyperscalers. ... CoreWeave depends on a few large customers for much of its revenue.

...

## One GPU, many price points

For an hour on an Nvidia H100 GPU, the range on 4 October 2026 is wide. The rates are only comparable to a limited extent. Lambda charges the equivalent of 3.55 euros for the H100 SXM, calculated at the European Central Bank (ECB) reference rate of 2 October 2026. Nebius has been charging the equivalent of 4.01 euros since 1 October 2026, and CoreWeave charges the equivalent of 43.87 euros for a node with eight H100s, which works out at 5.48 euros per GPU. In the US East region, AWS charges the equivalent of 6.13 euros per GPU hour for the p5.48xlarge instance with eight H100s, according to the price tracker Vantage as of 3 October 2026. For the Azure VM ND96isr H100 v5, AzureSpeed lists the equivalent of 10.95 euros per GPU hour as of 26 September 2026 for Linux with usage-based billing in East US.

Scaleway has been charging 25.332 euros per hour for a node with eight H100 SXM since 1 June 2026, which works out at 3.17 euros per GPU. OVHcloud lists the H100 as a PCIe card at 2.80 euros net, while Lambda and Scaleway quote the SXM form factor.

...

On 1 October 2026, Nebius raised the H100 hour from the equivalent of 3.43 to 4.01 euros, and the B200 from 6.37 to 7.57 euros. On 17 September 2026, CoreWeave reported short-duration contracts of three to six months at roughly 36 million euros in revenue per megawatt per year.

results.title: Scaleway Review 2026: What the European Cloud Costs After the June Price Rise | The Proof Desk
results.author: The Proof Desk Team
highlights:
On 1 June 2026 Scaleway raised prices for the first time in three years. It blamed rising RAM and storage hardware costs and the global IPv4 shortage. The smallest instance now costs four times what it did, every flexible IPv4 address went up 25%, and GPUs rose by roughly 5-10%. Over the same months Dedibox and Elastic Metal got cheaper, B300 GPUs arrived and Milan opened, so the picture is mixed rather than simply worse.

...

- Best for: EU-based startups, AI teams that want per-minute H100 billing in Europe, and anyone who needs data kept out of US jurisdiction.
- Watch out for: IPv4 and block storage billed on top of every instance, low quotas until you verify your identity, paid support for fast responses, and no hard spending cap.
- Prices in this review are in euros excluding VAT, taken from Scaleway's pricing pages on 3 October 2026.

## What changed in the June 2026 price increase

Scaleway announced the rise in an April 2026 blog post titled "A transparent update on Scaleway pricing". It says the company had "proudly held our prices flat" for three years, and that anything not on its list keeps its old price. These are the changes most customers will notice:

- STARDUST1-S: €0.00015 to €0.0006 an hour (4x, roughly €0.11 to €0.44 a month).
- DEV1-S: €0.0088 to €0.00898 an hour; DEV1-M €0.0198 to €0.0202; DEV1-L €0.042 to €0.04284.
- PLAY2-PICO: €0.014 to €0.01428; PRO2-XXS: €0.055 to €0.0561 an hour.
- Flexible IPv4: €0.004 to €0.005 an hour. The same increase applies to Bare Metal, Public Gateway and Load Balancer IPs.
- H100-1-80G: €2.73 to €2.87 an hour; H100-SXM-8-80G: €23.03 to €25.33; L40S-1-48G: €1.40 to €1.47; L4-1-24G: €0.75 to €0.79.
- Block Storage SSD: €0.000118 to €0.00013 per GB per hour; Object Storage Multi-AZ: €0.00002 to €0.000022.
- Load Balancer GP-S: €0.016 to €0.023 an hour; Public Gateway S: €0.0199 to €0.026; DNS zone for external domains: €0.001 to €0.007.
- Serverless Functions: €0.000012 to €0.000017 per GB-second.
- Elastic Metal EM-I220E-NVMe: €199.99 to €229.99 a month; Dedibox Core-10-XS: €119.99 to €134.99.

...

The changes that hurt sit around the instance rather than in it: IPv4, load balancers, gateways and DNS zones went up between 30% and 600%. A small stack with a load balancer and a gateway now costs noticeably more than it did in May, even if its instances barely changed.

...

### Billing rules worth knowing

- CPU instances are billed per hour of uptime, including startup and standby time. Each resource has a 60-minute minimum.
- GPU instances are billed per minute, except RENDER-S, which is billed per hour.
- Public IPs and volumes are billed for the whole time they are allocated, "regardless of whether the Instance is powered off." Powering off does not make a server free. You have to delete the IP and the volumes.
- Savings Plans promise up to 25% off compute if you commit to a monthly spend.

...

Monthly Dedibox subscriptions are charged pro rata for the first month and then in full at the start of each month. Elastic Metal can be rented by the hour, which suits short benchmarks or bursty batch jobs better than a classic dedicated server.

## GPUs and Generative APIs

Scaleway is one of the few EU-owned providers that sells H100 and B300 capacity on demand, billed per minute:

- L4-1-24G: €0.79/h (about €575/month), in PAR-1, PAR-2 and WAW-2.
- L40S-1-48G: about €1.47/h.
- H100-1-80G: about €2.87/h; H100-2-80G about €5.73/h.
- H100-SXM-8-80G: about €25.33/h (about €18,491/month).
- B300-SXM-8-288G: €60.00/h, PAR-2 only.
- No H200 or B200 instances are listed.

Generative APIs is the serverless model hosting service. It is priced per million tokens (input/output): gpt-oss-120b at €0.15/€0.60, Mistral Small 3.2 at €0.15/€0.35, Llama 3.3 70B at €0.90/€0.90, Qwen3 235B at €0.75/€2.25 and Mistral Medium 3.5 at €1.50/€7.50. Whisper transcription costs €0.003 per audio minute. New accounts get 1 million free tokens and 60 minutes of transcription, and the Batch API halves the price.

Two cautions apply. Dedicated Deployment (formerly Managed Inference) costs more than renting the same GPU yourself, for example €3.40 an hour for an H100 against about €2.87. And Scaleway retires serverless models fairly quickly: several, including Devstral 2, Pixtral and Qwen 3 Coder, were marked for end of life in July 2026. Pin model names and plan for migrations.

...

### How are Scaleway GPU instances billed?

Per minute of uptime, except RENDER-S, which is billed per hour. An H100-1-80G costs about €2.87 an hour and an eight-GPU H100 SXM node about €25.33. Stop and delete the instance when a job ends, because attached IPs and volumes keep billing.

results.title: European providers rent an NVIDIA H100 for roughly half the on-demand price of AWS and Azure. | Lindstead
results.author: Lindstead
highlights:
# European providers rent an NVIDIA H100 for roughly half the on-demand price of AWS and Azure. | Lindstead · LinkedIn · 2026-10-01T00:00:00+00:00

**Lindstead**.

---

European providers rent an NVIDIA H100 for roughly half the on-demand price of AWS and Azure.

On-demand price of one H100 per hour:
• OVHcloud (FR): about €2.62
• Verda (FI): €3.09
• Nebius (NL): €3.95 from today, €3.38 until yesterday
• AWS (US): €6.03
• Microsoft Azure (US): €6.12
• Google Cloud (US): €9.71

Scaleway (FR) lists from €2.73.

Price is only half of the comparison. Jurisdiction follows ownership, regardless of where the data centre stands:
• Under the US CLOUD Act, US companies can be compelled to hand over data they control, wherever it is stored.
• Dedicated "sovereign" offerings of US providers remain owned by the US parent.

For workloads where that exposure matters, an EU-headquartered provider removes the question. On these list prices, it also costs less.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

The full issue, with every provider's lowest observed price and the method notes, is here:
https://lnkd.in/efqfwQWm

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
results.author: Axis Intelligence Research
highlights:
> Prices verified on October 2, 2026. Every price on this page was read from the vendor’s live pricing page, public price API or retail listing on that date. AWS Capacity Block rates effective October 7, 2026 are taken from AWS’s own announcement on its pricing page.

...

## Quick Answer

How much does a GPU cost in October 2026? In the cloud, an NVIDIA H100 lists between $3.49 and $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand; the neocloud median is $3.99. A B200 lists from $6.69 to $8.60. On the consumer side, the cheapest new RTX 5070 on Newegg was $869.99 against a $549 launch price — 58% above MSRP.

...

1. According to Axis Intelligence Research, hyperscalers list the NVIDIA H100 at 2.93 times the neocloud median price — $11.68 versus $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, as of October 2, 2026 (GPU Hour Premium Ratio, GHPR).
2. AWS raises EC2 Capacity Block GPU rates about 15% effective October 7, 2026, taking an H100 accelerator-hour from $5.191 to $5.970 and a B200 from $12.355 to $14.208, per AWS’s pricing page.
3. An 8-GPU H100 server rented on-demand for three years costs $2.58 million on Azure and $734,000 on Runpod, according to Axis Intelligence Research’s list-price TCO calculation.
4. The cheapest new GeForce RTX 5070 on Newegg cost $869.99 on October 2, 2026, 58% above the $549 price NVIDIA announced at CES in January 2025.
5. Azure’s spot price for an 8x H100 VM is 82% below its own on-demand rate — $18.17 versus $98.32 per hour in US East, per Microsoft’s Retail Prices API.

...

### H100 on-demand price per GPU-hour by provider (October 2, 2026)

| Provider | Instance / SKU | Listed price | GPUs | Price per GPU-hour | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod | H100 SXM Pod (Secure Cloud) | $3.49/hr | 1 | $3.49 | Runpod pricing |
| Lambda | NVIDIA H100 SXM instance | $3.99/GPU/hr | 1–8 | $3.99 | Lambda pricing |
| CoreWeave | NVIDIA HGX H100 (North America) | $49.24/hr | 8 | $6.16 | CoreWeave pricing |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g, us-central1 | $88.49/hr | 8 | $11.06 | Google Cloud accelerator-optimized pricing |
| Microsoft Azure | ND96isr H100 v5, East US | $98.32/hr | 8 | $12.29 | Azure Retail Prices API |

...

AWS’s per-accelerator figure that we verified is the EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML rate — a reservation you book for a fixed window, not open-ended on-demand. On October 2, 2026 the p5.48xlarge (8x H100) Capacity Block rate in US East (N. Virginia) was $41.528 per instance-hour, or $5.191 per H100. AWS’s pricing page states that from October 7, 2026, the P5 rate becomes $5.970 per accelerator across all available regions. Axis Intelligence Research did not verify a current AWS on-demand p5 rate for this snapshot, so AWS is excluded from the on-demand table rather than estimated.

...

AWS publishes the reason in one line: Capacity Block reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand. The October 7, 2026 update moves every GPU family up by the same proportion.

results.title: Nebius October Price Increase: Recalculate Startup Runway | Lunera
highlights:
Nebius’s October 1, 2026 on-demand GPU price increases are now effective, with H100, H200, B200 and B300 rates up roughly 17%–21%. Recalculate startup runway using the additional cost of exposed usage—not the headline percentage. A 20% GPU price increase does not mean a 20% increase in company burn, and the price change alone is not a reason to migrate.

...

Source: Nebius public USD on-demand prices, as cited for October 6, 2026. Old → new: H100 $3.85 → $4.50; H200 $4.50 → $5.40; B200 $7.15 → $8.50; B300 $7.85 → $9.50 per GPU-hour.

## The Increase Applies To Specific Resources And Rates

As of October 6, 2026, Nebius’s public pricing page lists these USD on-demand rates per GPU-hour. Percentage increases are calculated from those prices.

| GPU | Old Rate | New Rate | Increase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | 16.9% |
| H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | 20.0% |
| B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | 18.9% |
| B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | 21.0% |

These are per GPU, not per multi-GPU VM, and exclude applicable taxes. The same page shows unchanged on-demand rates for RTX PRO 6000 and unchanged starting prices for L40S configurations.

The change also reaches some CPU-only workloads. Nebius’s compute documentation identifies increases for non-GPU AMD Epyc Genoa CPU and RAM, and non-GPU Intel Ice Lake RAM. Audit those resources separately; do not apply a blanket GPU percentage to the whole invoice. The figures above do not quantify the CPU and RAM increases.

results.title: Nebius and CoreWeave Lift Nvidia GPU Prices by Up to 21% – Swing To Trade
highlights:
Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue. A landlord can charge more for a chip it does not make only while that chip stays scarce. That is the signal behind Nvidia, and it is the opposite of a capacity glut.

Nebius’s price page, checked on October 2, still prints two columns. On-demand H100 is $3.85 per GPU-hour. The column marked effective October 1 is $4.50. The same split runs through the H200, the B200, and the B300. Reuters reported on September 17 that this was the second pay-as-you-go increase in about three months, with selected Nvidia GPU rates up 17% to 21%. The card on nebius.com/prices matches that range. It does not show every customer already paying the new rate.

## The card Nebius posted

Four Nvidia rows have a public before and after. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 racks are still “contact us” in both columns. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. L40S “from” rates do not move. The hike lands on the accelerators customers are queued for.

| Nvidia GPU | Prior on-demand column | Announced October 1 card | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HGX H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | +$0.65, or 16.9% |
| HGX H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | +$0.90, or 20.0% |
| HGX B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | +$1.35, or 18.9% |
| HGX B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | +$1.65, or 21.0% |

Reuters’ “17% to 21%” is this range, with 16.9% rounded up. “Up to 21%” is the B300. The smaller H100 move is the one that changes the reading.

...

Announced Nebius on-demand rates for October 1, 2026, set against the prior on-demand column still printed on the same page. These are posted card rates, not a receipt. The live page and a third-party tracker still disagree, so this chart does not show what every customer is paying. Source: nebius.com/prices, checked October 2, 2026.

...

## The announced column is not yet the only column

October 2 is after the effective date, and the page still shows both numbers. The left-hand label is still “On-demand, GPU-hour.” The right-hand label is “GPU-hour (Effective October 1, 2026).” A customer cannot tell, from the page alone, which figure the console will bill.

GPU Finder’s Nebius page, with availability checked at 06:23 UTC on October 2, still listed one-GPU on-demand rates of $3.85 for the H100, $7.15 for the B200, and $7.85 for the B300. Those are the old column. The same check already showed the H200 at $5.40, the new column, with a spot print of $2.45 beside it. The H100 spot print on that row was $2.15. The tracker has not frozen. It has moved one of the four headline GPUs and left the other three on the pre-October number. Treating the whole book as repriced at midnight on October 1 would be tidier, and it would be wrong.
